History of Present Illness:
Ms. ___ is a ___ yo female with Type II DM presented to the ED 
last night with ""heart racing"" and difficulty catching her 
breath. She reports that for the past week she has felt poor, 
with polyuria and polyphagia and overall weakness.The ""racing 
heart"" and SOB started while she was walking up a flight of 
stairs and came on gradually; she reports never having sx 
before. Her symptoms resolved spontaneously in the ED- she 
attributes this to getting fluid- and she denied chest pain. On 
arrival to the ED, she was found to have a critically high 
glucose of 717 on fingerstick with AG 18.  
.  
Ms. ___ was diagnosed with DMII in the 1990s and has 
consistently had poor control. She notes that she has not been 
hospitalized since first diagnosis, but is constantly 
readjusting her regimen with her physicians. She reports that 
she had not been taking her insulin or Metformin for a few weeks 
due to high costs (although she has insurance she finds the 
co-pays difficult to pay.) Of note, other providers report that 
Ms. ___ stated she has a needle phobia which prevents her from 
taking her insulin.  
.

ago

Brief Hospital Course:
Her ED course was significant for: Normal vital signs, 1000 
glucose and + ketones in urine; she was put on insulin gtt and 
3L fluid.  
.  
She was transferred to ICU still on insulin gtt and given 1 
additional liter IVF. Her anion gap closed quickly within a few 
hours and she was taken off the heparin gtt and placed on 
insulin standing Humalog ___ with 18U in am and 15U in pm with 
sliding scale. Fingersticks since 5 AM have ranged 84-240. Na 
(129), Mag and Phos were low on first set of labs; Na corrected 
with fluid administration and Mag and Phos were repleted in the 
ICU.
.
Ms. ___ was then transferred to the floor, where she continued 
to have normal vitals signs and mental status. Her blood sugars 
ranged in the 200s to 300s on ___. The ___ team came to see 
her and adjusted her standing insulin and recommended checking 
C-peptide. She was discharged on a regimen of 20 U Humalog ___ 
in the am and 22 U Humalog ___ in the pm with instructions to 
check blood sugars twice daily and followup with primary care 
doctor.She will also continue her Metformin and was called after 
discharge to confirm that she should continue this medication 
(it was inadvertently left off her discharge worksheet)
.
Social work spoke to Ms. ___ about her obstacles to taking 
insulin. She agreed that she does not want to be sick and will 
take her insulin if necessary- she said that her co-pays cost 
about $15 monthly. 
 
Medications on Admission:
- Paxil 50mg daily
- Trazodone QHS PRN
- Lisinopril 2.5mg PO daily

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital because you felt like your 
heart was racing and you had very very high blood glucose level. 
This happened because you were not taking your insulin. A very 
high blood glucose level can lead to dehydration- this is 
probably why you felt your heart racing- and can also change the 
levels of important chemicals (electrolytes) in your body. This 
can be very dangerous. Therefore, it is very important that you 
take your insulin as instructed and that you measure blood sugar 
regularly. If you have high blood sugar over a period of time, 
you can end up needing an amputation or even going blind. While 
you were here we involved the ___ to give us 
recommendations on what amount of insulin you should be taking 
at home. These were their recommendations: 
You should take 20 units of Humalog ___ in the morning and 22 
units of Humalog ___ at night. You should check your blood 
sugars twice a day- once in the morning before you eat anything 
and once at night. Please write these levels down to show to 
your primary care doctor. He will then adjust your insulin 
levels if needed.
